text:
ashley: gitleaks scheduled run flagged something in infra-legacy-modules/terraform/modules/old_kms/main.tf — looks like a base64 blob that matches our KMS-wrapped payload pattern. excerpt below:
```
module "old_kms" {
  secret_blob = "CiQA...BASE64...=="
}
```
ashley: attaching commit abc123 that introduced it, unknown author (service account)
gitleaks-bot: Scan result: possible KMS-wrapped-blob, rule_id=KMS_ENC_BLOB, path=modules/old_kms/main.tf, commit=abc123
mike: tagging @sophia @infra-oncall — do we treat as secret exposure? could be safe if truly KMS-wrapped, but need KMS audit and who decrypted it
sophia: on it. I'll pull Cloud KMS audit logs for key key-prod-legacy for last 90d and check decrypts. assigning to self
infra-oncall: quick check: key exists, primary key ring legacy-kr. No anomalous locations in metadata, but commit author is deploy-bot@redwood. That SA has been used by a 2019 CI runner before.
ryan: recommend immediate containment: rotate the key, revoke deploy-bot SA credentials, scan mirrors/artifacts for the blob, and prepare rollback/remove commit. Do not rewrite history until we know who pulled it.
julie: agree with ryan. create incident ticket before large-scale history rewrite. we also need to scope who could have accessed the repo (internal mirrors, archives, backups).
ashley: created incident INC-2026-032 and posted containment checklist in the ticket: 1) rotate KMS key 2) revoke SA keys for deploy-bot 3) scan mirrors & CI artifacts for blob 4) remove blob commit + consider revert vs history rewrite 5) notify infra/security owners. assigned owners in ticket.
sophia: KMS logs: found 2 Decrypt calls in last 30 days from project=ci-builds, principal=serviceAccount:deploy-runner@ci. The decrypts line up with two CI runs on 1987600100 and 1987620000. Suggest rotate immediately.
mike: starting key rotation now — command I'm running: 
```bash
gcloud kms keys versions create --key key-prod-legacy --location global --keyring legacy-kr --project=redwood-infra
```
infra-oncall: after rotation I removed cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter role from deploy-bot and added narrowly scoped Workload Identity mapping to ephemeral runners only. Also created temporary deny policy for legacy-kr until we confirm.
julie: scanning mirrors and artifact bucket for the exact base64 snippet. so far found a copy in mirror-archive (pulled 2019) and one build artifact in ci-artifacts/bucket-1 from 2020. initiating artifact deletion requests and access audit.
ashley: containment status: rotated key ✅, revoked SA JSONs ✅, artifact removal requests submitted ✅. still enumerating consumers who may have pulled the mirror. marking as contained for now. :white_check_mark:
ryan: post-incident action items draft: - enforce pre-commit secret detection on legacy repo - add hook to block large base64 blobs in .tf files - require signed commits on main branches - increase KMS audit log retention to 1y - run retro focused on detection-coverage and RBAC around KMS keys
mike: I'll open the pre-commit + CI PR for the blob rule and an infra change to block pushes without branch protection. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123
sophia: also adding a KMS runbook for these detections: steps to triage decrypt logs, rotate keys safely (minimal downtime), and communication checklist. will add to runbooks/docs repo.
julie: note for retro: check whether we can limit long-lived service accounts in legacy repos, and backfill repository-level branch protections across archive mirrors.
ashley: closing loop for now — incident INC-2026-032 set to contained, follow-ups assigned in ticket. we'll run a 1-week follow-up to confirm no external access. thanks everyone.
infra-oncall: will push remediation summary to #incidents and archive findings in ticket.
ashley: posting small retro agenda in INC ticket and scheduling a 30m sync for tomorrow 10:00 PST to finalize action owners.
